sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity
sources.locator: §3.2.5, printed pp. 113–117 (PDF pp. 120–124): curved-space Maxwell action, sourced form equation, charge and Stokes flux; §4.5.3, printed pp. 183–186 (PDF pp. 191–194): Maxwell stress tensor and observer energy density; §4.5.5, printed pp. 187–188 (PDF pp. 194–195): finite-region charge balance and boundary-current qualification. contents.name: Curved Maxwell form equation and gauge-current condition
contents.support: Independent treatment of the differential-form source equation, the current-conservation condition, and its covariant-divergence encoding. Tong uses natural units and a different displayed source normalization/sign convention; only the structural comparison was used. The carrier derives the run's SI signs from its exact planned mathematical interface.

contents.name: Charge definition and finite-boundary Gauss flux
contents.support: Supports the charge-as-current-flux and Stokes conversion to field flux. The local item states the SI factor 1/(mu0 c), finite smooth-chain hypotheses, and the limitation to bounding surfaces explicitly.

contents.name: Maxwell stress tensor and field energy density
contents.locator: §4.5.3, printed pp. 183–186 (PDF pp. 191–194), equation (4.52) and the flat-space T00 computation
contents.support: Independent check of the quadratic tensor structure and positive pure-electric energy density. Tong suppresses SI constants; the example uses the exact planned observer-stress supplier and retains epsilon0 and mu0.

contents.name: Finite-region charge conservation and side flux
contents.support: Confirms that constant charge in a region requires zero or included side flux. The item retains the exact side-flux identity and makes no unsupported decay claim at infinity.

sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1
sources.locator: Chapter 1, printed pp. 20–24 (PDF pp. 26–30): tensor Maxwell equations and differential-form encoding; Chapter 1, printed pp. 29–30 (PDF pp. 35–36): electromagnetic stress tensor; Chapter 4, printed pp. 107–108 (PDF pp. 113–114): curved-spacetime Maxwell equations and the relation between covariant and exterior derivatives. Relevant derivations and qualifications read in full.

contents.name: Tensor Maxwell equations from the four spatial equations
contents.support: Independent component derivation of the tensor Maxwell equations from electric and magnetic components. Carroll uses Gaussian units and its own index/sign conventions; no coefficient or sign is imported.

contents.name: Maxwell equations as differential-form identities
contents.support: Independent treatment of dF=0 and the sourced Hodge-dual equation. The exact adopted SI current form and its orientation sign are derived locally.

contents.name: Curved-spacetime Maxwell equations and connection cancellation
contents.support: Independent curved-spacetime discussion of covariant and exterior formulations, including the antisymmetry/torsion-free cancellation. The item conditions its result on the adopted curved Maxwell postulate and the exact planned coordinate-form lemma.
